NASB.1: Now Abraham journeyed from there toward the land of the Negev, and settled between Kadesh and Shur; then he sojourned in Gerar.
NASB.2: Abraham said of Sarah his wife, 'She is my sister.' So Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.
NASB.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night, and said to him, 'Behold, you are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken, for she is married.'
NASB.4: Now Abimelech had not come near her; and he said, 'Lord, will You slay a nation, even [though] blameless?
NASB.5: 'Did he not himself say to me, 'She is my sister '? And she herself said, 'He is my brother.' In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this.'
NASB.6: Then God said to him in the dream, 'Yes, I know that in the integrity of your heart you have done this, and I also kept you from sinning against Me; therefore I did not let you touch her.
NASB.7: 'Now therefore, restore the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not restore [her], know that you shall surely die, you and all who are yours.'
NASB.8: So Abimelech arose early in the morning and called all his servants and told all these things in their hearing; and the men were greatly frightened.
NASB.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, 'What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done to me things that ought not to be done.'
NASB.10: And Abimelech said to Abraham, 'What have you encountered, that you have done this thing?'
NASB.11: Abraham said, 'Because I thought, surely there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.
NASB.12: 'Besides, she actually is my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife;
NASB.13: and it came about, when God caused me to wander from my father's house, that I said to her, 'This is the kindness which you will show to me: everywhere we go, say of me, 'He is my brother.'''
NASB.14: Abimelech then took sheep and oxen and male and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and restored his wife Sarah to him.
NASB.15: Abimelech said, 'Behold, my land is before you; settle wherever you please.'
NASB.16: To Sarah he said, 'Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver; behold, it is your vindication before all who are with you, and before all men you are cleared.'
NASB.17: Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his maids, so that they bore [children].
NASB.18: For the LORD had closed fast all the wombs of the household of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

ESV.1: From there Abraham journeyed toward the territory of the Negeb and lived between Kadesh and Shur; and he sojourned in Gerar.
ESV.2: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” And Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.
ESV.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said to him, “Behold, you are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken, for she is a man's wife.”
ESV.4: Now Abimelech had not approached her. So he said, “Lord, will you kill an innocent people?
ESV.5: Did he not himself say to me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this.”
ESV.6: Then God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that you have done this in the integrity of your heart, and it was I who kept you from sinning against me. Therefore I did not let you touch her.
ESV.7: Now then, return the man's wife, for he is a prophet, so that he will pray for you, and you shall live. But if you do not return her, know that you shall surely die, you and all who are yours.”
ESV.8: So Abimelech rose early in the morning and called all his servants and told them all these things. And the men were very much afraid.
ESV.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, “What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and my kingdom a great sin? You have done to me things that ought not to be done.”
ESV.10: And Abimelech said to Abraham, “What did you see, that you did this thing?”
ESV.11: Abraham said, “I did it because I thought, ‘There is no fear of God at all in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.’
ESV.12: Besides, she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father though not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife.
ESV.13: And when God caused me to wander from my father's house, I said to her, ‘This is the kindness you must do me: at every place to which we come, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
ESV.14: Then Abimelech took sheep and oxen, and male servants and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and returned Sarah his wife to him.
ESV.15: And Abimelech said, “Behold, my land is before you; dwell where it pleases you.”
ESV.16: To Sarah he said, “Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. It is a sign of your innocence in the eyes of all  who are with you, and before everyone you are vindicated.”
ESV.17: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, and also healed his wife and female slaves so that they bore children.
ESV.18: For the LORD had closed all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

NKJV.6: And God said to him in a dream, “Yes, I know that you did this in the integrity of your heart. For I also withheld you from sinning against Me; therefore I did not let you touch her.

NKJV.18: for the LORD had closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

NLT.1: Abraham moved south to the Negev and lived for a while between Kadesh and Shur, and then he moved on to Gerar. While living there as a foreigner,
NLT.2: Abraham introduced his wife, Sarah, by saying, “She is my sister.” So King Abimelech of Gerar sent for Sarah and had her brought to him at his palace.
NLT.3: But that night God came to Abimelech in a dream and told him, “You are a dead man, for that woman you have taken is already married!”
NLT.4: But Abimelech had not slept with her yet, so he said, “Lord, will you destroy an innocent nation?
NLT.5: Didn’t Abraham tell me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘Yes, he is my brother.’ I acted in complete innocence! My hands are clean.”
NLT.6: In the dream God responded, “Yes, I know you are innocent. That’s why I kept you from sinning against me, and why I did not let you touch her.
NLT.7: Now return the woman to her husband, and he will pray for you, for he is a prophet. Then you will live. But if you don’t return her to him, you can be sure that you and all your people will die.”
NLT.8: Abimelech got up early the next morning and quickly called all his servants together. When he told them what had happened, his men were terrified.
NLT.9: Then Abimelech called for Abraham. “What have you done to us?” he demanded. “What crime have I committed that deserves treatment like this, making me and my kingdom guilty of this great sin? No one should ever do what you have done!
NLT.10: Whatever possessed you to do such a thing?”
NLT.11: Abraham replied, “I thought, ‘This is a godless place. They will want my wife and will kill me to get her.’
NLT.12: And she really is my sister, for we both have the same father, but different mothers. And I married her.
NLT.13: When God called me to leave my father’s home and to travel from place to place, I told her, ‘Do me a favor. Wherever we go, tell the people that I am your brother.’”
NLT.14: Then Abimelech took some of his sheep and goats, cattle, and male and female servants, and he presented them to Abraham. He also returned his wife, Sarah, to him.
NLT.15: Then Abimelech said, “Look over my land and choose any place where you would like to live.”
NLT.16: And he said to Sarah, “Look, I am giving your ‘brother’ 1,000 pieces of silver in the presence of all these witnesses. This is to compensate you for any wrong I may have done to you. This will settle any claim against me, and your reputation is cleared.”
NLT.17: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, so they could have children.
NLT.18: For the LORD had caused all the women to be infertile because of what happened with Abraham’s wife, Sarah.

WEB.1: Abraham traveled from there toward the land of the South, and lived between Kadesh and Shur. He lived as a foreigner in Gerar.
WEB.2: Abraham said about Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
WEB.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night, and said to him, “Behold, you are a dead man, because of the woman whom you have taken. For she is a man’s wife.”
WEB.4: Now Abimelech had not come near her. He said, “Lord, will you kill even a righteous nation?
WEB.5: Didn’t he tell me, ‘She is my sister?’ She, even she herself, said, ‘He is my brother.’ In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this.”
WEB.6: God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that in the integrity of your heart you have done this, and I also withheld you from sinning against me. Therefore I didn’t allow you to touch her.
WEB.7: Now therefore, restore the man’s wife. For he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you will live. If you don’t restore her, know for sure that you will die, you, and all who are yours.”
WEB.8: Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ear. The men were very scared.
WEB.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that ought not to be done!”
WEB.10: Abimelech said to Abraham, “What did you see, that you have done this thing?”
WEB.11: Abraham said, “Because I thought, ‘Surely the fear of God is not in this place. They will kill me for my wife’s sake.’
WEB.12: Besides, she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.
WEB.13: When God caused me to wander from my father’s house, I said to her, ‘This is your kindness which you shall show to me. Everywhere that we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
WEB.14: Abimelech took sheep and cattle, male servants and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and restored Sarah, his wife, to him.
WEB.15: Abimelech said, “Behold, my land is before you. Dwell where it pleases you.”
WEB.16: To Sarah he said, “Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. Behold, it is for you a covering of the eyes to all that are with you. In front of all you are vindicated.”
WEB.17: Abraham prayed to God. God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his female servants, and they bore children.
WEB.18: For Yahweh had closed up tight all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

AMP.1: Now Abraham journeyed from there toward the Negev (the South country), and settled between Kadesh and Shur; then he lived temporarily in Gerar.
AMP.2: Abraham said [again] of Sarah his wife, "She is my sister." So Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah [into his harem].
AMP.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream during the night, and said, "Behold, you are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken [as your wife], for she is another man's wife."
AMP.4: Now Abimelech had not yet come near her; so he said, "Lord, will you kill a people who are righteous and innocent and blameless [regarding Sarah]?
AMP.5: Did Abraham not tell me, 'She is my sister?' And she herself said, 'He is my brother.' In the integrity of my heart and innocence of my hands I have done this."
AMP.6: Then God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know you did this in the integrity of your heart, for it was I who kept you back and spared you from sinning against Me; therefore I did not give you an opportunity to touch her.
AMP.7: So now return the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not return her [to him], know that you shall die, you and all who are yours (your household)."
AMP.8: So Abimelech got up early in the morning and called all his servants and told them all these things; and the men were terrified.
AMP.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, "What have you done to us? And how have I offended you that you have brought on me and my kingdom a great sin? You have done to me what ought not to be done [to anyone]."
AMP.10: And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What have you encountered or seen [in us or our customs], that you have done this [unjust] thing?"
AMP.11: Abraham said, "Because I thought, 'Surely there is no fear or reverence of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.'
AMP.12: Besides, she actually is my [half] sister; she is the daughter of my father [Terah], but not of my mother; and she became my wife.
AMP.13: When God caused me to wander from my father's house, I said to her, 'This kindness and loyalty you can show me: at every place we stop, say of me, "He is my brother."'"
AMP.14: Then Abimelech took sheep and oxen and male and female slaves, and gave them to Abraham, and returned Sarah his wife to him [as God commanded].
AMP.15: So Abimelech said, "Behold, my land is before you; settle wherever you please."
AMP.16: Then to Sarah he said, "Look, I have given this brother of yours a thousand pieces of silver; it is to compensate you [for all that has happened] and to vindicate your honor before all who are with you; before all men you are cleared and compensated."
AMP.17: So Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his maids, and they again gave birth to children,
AMP.18: for the LORD had securely closed the wombs of all [the women] in Abimelech's household because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

CSB17.6: Then God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that you did this with a clear conscience. <sup>[4]</sup> I have also kept you from sinning against me. Therefore I have not let you touch her.

CSB17.16: And he said to Sarah, “Look, I am giving your brother one thousand pieces of silver. It is a verification of your honor <sup>[7]</sup> to all who are with you. You are fully vindicated.”

CSB17.18: for the LORD had completely closed all the wombs in Abimelech’s household on account of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

NRSVCE.1: From there Abraham journeyed toward the region of the Negeb, and settled between Kadesh and Shur. While residing in Gerar as an alien,

NRSVCE.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said to him, “You are about to die because of the woman whom you have taken; for she is a married woman.”
NRSVCE.4: Now Abimelech had not approached her; so he said, “Lord, will you destroy an innocent people?
NRSVCE.5: Did he not himself say to me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ I did this in the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands.”
NRSVCE.6: Then God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that you did this in the integrity of your heart; furthermore it was I who kept you from sinning against me. Therefore I did not let you touch her.

NRSVCE.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought such great guilt on me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that ought not to be done.”

NIV.1:
Abraham and Abimelech
Now Abraham moved on from there into the region of the Negev and lived between Kadesh and Shur. For a while he stayed in Gerar,
NIV.2: and there Abraham said of his wife Sarah, “She is my sister.” Then Abimelech king of Gerar sent for Sarah and took her.
NIV.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream one night and said to him, “You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken; she is a married woman.”
NIV.4: Now Abimelech had not gone near her, so he said, “Lord, will you destroy an innocent nation?
NIV.5: Did he not say to me, ‘She is my sister,’ and didn’t she also say, ‘He is my brother’? I have done this with a clear conscience and clean hands.”
NIV.6: Then God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know you did this with a clear conscience, and so I have kept you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
NIV.7: Now return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not return her, you may be sure that you and all yours will die.”
NIV.8: Early the next morning Abimelech summoned all his officials, and when he told them all that had happened, they were very much afraid.
NIV.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham in and said, “What have you done to us? How have I wronged you that you have brought such great guilt upon me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not be done.”
NIV.10: And Abimelech asked Abraham, “What was your reason for doing this?”
NIV.11: Abraham replied, “I said to myself, ‘There is surely no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.’
NIV.12: Besides, she really is my sister, the daughter of my father though not of my mother; and she became my wife.
NIV.13: And when God had me wander from my father’s household, I said to her, ‘This is how you can show your love to me: Everywhere we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
NIV.14: Then Abimelech brought sheep and cattle and male and female slaves and gave them to Abraham, and he returned Sarah his wife to him.
NIV.15: And Abimelech said, “My land is before you; live wherever you like.”
NIV.16: To Sarah he said, “I am giving your brother a thousand shekels of silver. This is to cover the offense against you before all who are with you; you are completely vindicated.”
NIV.17: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife and his slave girls so they could have children again,
NIV.18: for the Lord had closed up every womb in Abimelech’s household because of Abraham’s wife Sarah.

NET.1: Abraham journeyed from there to the Negev region and settled between Kadesh and Shur. While he lived as a temporary resident in Gerar,
NET.2: Abraham said about his wife Sarah, “She is my sister.” So Abimelech, king of Gerar, sent for Sarah and took her.
NET.3: But God appeared to Abimelech in a dream at night and said to him, “You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken, for she is someone else’s wife.”
NET.4: Now Abimelech had not gone near her. He said, “Lord, would you really slaughter an innocent nation?
NET.5: Did Abraham not say to me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ I have done this with a clear conscience and with innocent hands!”
NET.6: Then in the dream God replied to him, “Yes, I know that you have done this with a clear conscience. That is why I have kept you from sinning against me and why I did not allow you to touch her.
NET.7: But now give back the man’s wife. Indeed he is a prophet and he will pray for you; thus you will live. But if you don’t give her back, know that you will surely die along with all who belong to you.”
NET.8: Early in the morning Abimelech summoned all his servants. When he told them about all these things, they were terrified.
NET.9: Abimelech summoned Abraham and said to him, “What have you done to us? What sin did I commit against you that would cause you to bring such great guilt on me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not be done!”
NET.10: Then Abimelech asked Abraham, “What prompted you to do this thing?”
NET.11: Abraham replied, “Because I thought, ‘Surely no one fears God in this place. They will kill me because of my wife.’
NET.12: What’s more, she is indeed my sister, my father’s daughter, but not my mother’s daughter. She became my wife.
NET.13: When God made me wander from my father’s house, I told her, ‘This is what you can do to show your loyalty to me: Every place we go, say about me, “He is my brother.”’”
NET.14: So Abimelech gave sheep, cattle, and male and female servants to Abraham. He also gave his wife Sarah back to him.
NET.15: Then Abimelech said, “Look, my land is before you; live wherever you please.”
NET.16: To Sarah he said, “Look, I have given a thousand pieces of silver to your ‘brother.’ This is compensation for you so that you will stand vindicated before all who are with you.”
NET.17: Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, as well as his wife and female slaves so that they were able to have children.
NET.18: For the LORD had caused infertility to strike every woman in the household of Abimelech because he took Sarah, Abraham’s wife.
